seo.title: Apple Maps Place Card: Complete It for Your Business
seo.meta_description: How to complete your Apple Maps place card in Apple Business: header, display name rules, about section and attributes, for Orange County businesses.

h1: The Apple Maps Place Card: How to Complete Every Section
answer: The Apple Maps place card is the panel customers see when they select your business in Apple Maps, and Apple says it also appears in Siri, Calendar, Messages and more. In Apple Business you can add a header with logo and cover photo, set a display name that matches your signage, write an about section and configure attributes. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should complete every part.
key_takeaways: The place card appears across Apple apps.
The header is your logo plus cover photo.
The display name must match your signage.
No symbols like ® or ™ in the name.
Apple reviews content against its guidelines.

sections.heading: Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business
sections.body_html: Apple's guide states that Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business, which combines what was previously in Apple Business Manager, Apple Business Essentials and Apple Business Connect into one offering. If you used Apple Business Connect before, you can sign in to Apple Business with the same personal Apple Account.

sections.heading: What the place card is
sections.body_html: Apple's guide describes the place card as the starting point for your location information, appearing across Apple's software from Maps to Siri, Calendar and Messages. As you add photos, showcases and details, it becomes a true extension of your physical location.

sections.heading: Add a header
sections.body_html: The header combines your brand logo and a cover photo. In Apple Business, choose Brands, Locations, select the location, then Info. Upload or confirm your logo, add a cover photo, move and resize it, and select Add. Apple reviews the images before they appear.

sections.heading: Display name rules
sections.body_html:
• Must match the name on your storefront, signage or official website.
  • No descriptions or extra words.
  • No symbols such as ®, © or ™, and no semicolons, braces or brackets.
  • Periods, commas, hyphens, apostrophes and parentheses are allowed when part of the brand name.
  • A city can appear only if it's part of the actual brand name.

sections.heading: City names in names
sections.body_html: Apple's example: Stella Coffee Beverly Hills is fine if that's the brand name, but adding a city to tell locations apart, such as Smith's Family Restaurant (Fresno, CA), isn't allowed. The same applies to businesses with several Orange County locations.

sections.heading: Languages
sections.body_html: Apple says the display name needs a correctly specified language, and you can add names in other languages as long as they're consistent. That helps businesses serving Orange County's Spanish, Vietnamese and Korean-speaking communities.

sections.heading: The about section
sections.body_html: Apple calls the about section an opportunity to tell Apple about the location; it's displayed on the place card. Apple's examples include information about who you are, such as family-run or owned by a particular community, and credentials. It must follow Apple's photo and text standards.

sections.heading: Keep content accurate
sections.body_html: Apple reviews content against its standards and guidelines. Write plainly, avoid promotional claims in the name, and keep hours and status current, since customers can report inaccuracies.

sections.heading: Match your other listings
sections.body_html: Use the same name, address, phone, hours and website on Apple Maps as on your Google Business Profile and website. Consistency helps customers and the many apps and assistants that read business data.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Adding keywords or a city to the display name.
  • Using ® or ™ in the name.
  • Leaving the about section empty.
  • No cover photo, so the header looks bare.
  • Different hours from Google.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether adding services or a city to the name helps them rank on Apple Maps. Apple's guidelines don't allow it, and it can delay approval; put services and areas in the about section and your website instead. Another question is how long changes take to appear. Images and some changes are reviewed by Apple first, so allow a few days and check back. Owners also ask whether the place card matters if most customers use Google. Many iPhone users tap addresses in Messages, Calendar or Siri suggestions, which open Apple's place card, so it's often seen more than owners expect, especially by visitors to Anaheim who use their phones to find places nearby.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Logo and cover photo approved.
  • Display name matches signage.
  • No symbols or keywords in the name.
  • About section written.
  • Languages set correctly.
  • Details match Google.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a Vietnamese restaurant in Westminster whose Apple Maps name includes Best Pho Little Saigon. The owner changes the display name to the name on the sign, adds a Vietnamese-language name, writes an about section mentioning that it's family-run since 1998, and uploads a logo and cover photo of the dining room.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: It helps to see where this sits in the bigger picture. Google ranks local results mainly on relevance, distance and popularity, and AI assistants lean on the same public information: your Business Profile, your website, other listings and what customers write. For a business in Anaheim or anywhere in Orange County, the most reliable plan is simple and repeated: keep every listing accurate, explain each service clearly on its own page, show real proof of your work and reply to customers. Small improvements here compound, and they are far harder for competitors to copy than an ad budget.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Open Info for your location.
  2. Fix the display name.
  3. Write the about section.
  4. Upload a logo and cover photo.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Plenty of owners handle this themselves. Outside help pays off when time is short, when the business has many locations or when a problem is costing calls every day it stays unresolved. Be wary of anyone who promises guaranteed positions or asks for your verification codes or passwords; Google says nobody can pay for a better local ranking. Look for clear explanations, honest timelines and reporting tied to real enquiries. Chimera offers exactly that to businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County.

sections.heading: How to write the about section
sections.body_html: Keep the about section short, specific and factual. Start with what you do and for whom, such as Family-run bakery making sourdough and custom cakes since 2009. Add what makes you different: languages spoken, certifications, specialties or community ties. Avoid superlatives such as best in Orange County, prices that change often and phone numbers or links, which belong in other fields. Write in the same voice as your website and Google Business Profile description so customers get a consistent picture. If you serve customers in several languages, add the about text in each language you support, keeping the meaning consistent. Review it once a year or whenever your services change, and update it at the same time as your other listings.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Add a logo and cover photo, use your real signage name, write a clear about section and keep details matching Google. Chimera, based in Anaheim, completes Apple place cards for Orange County businesses.

faqs.q: What is an Apple Maps place card?
faqs.a: The panel with your business details shown in Maps, Siri, Calendar, Messages and more.

faqs.q: Can I add keywords to my Apple Maps name?
faqs.a: No. Apple says the name must match your signage with no descriptions.
No. Apple says those symbols aren't allowed.

faqs.q: Can I add a city to my name?
faqs.a: Only if it's part of the actual brand name.

faqs.q: What goes in the about section?
faqs.a: Information about your business, following Apple's text guidelines.

faqs.q: Does Apple review place card content?
faqs.a: Yes, images and content are reviewed against its guidelines.

faqs.q: Do you help businesses in Anaheim and Orange County with this?
faqs.a: Yes. Chimera is based in Anaheim, California and works with businesses across Orange County, California.
